original.target_description: Problem 3: Strength of emotion: Trish below goal versus Sally above goal.

es.quote:
Problem 3. [N ⫽ 48] Sally and Trish both follow workout plans that usually
     involve doing 25 sit-ups.
        One day, Sally sets a goal of performing 31 sit-ups. She finds herself very tired
     after performing 35 sit-ups and stops.
        Trish sets a goal of performing 39 sit-ups. She finds herself very tired after per-
     forming 35 sit-ups and stops.
        Who is experiencing more emotion? Sally (29%) Trish (71%)

    As in Problem 1, if we ask participants which emotion Sally and Trish
are experiencing, they agree unanimously that Trish is feeling negative emo-
tion and Sally is feeling positive emotion. In addition, a majority of partici-
pants agree that Trish is feeling stronger emotion than Sally (p ⬍ .05 by
χ 2 ).

notes: Sally 29% and Trish 71%, with p < .05 by chi-square; the numeric test statistic is not printed. Only assigned fields are completion targets; remaining entries are placeholders or supplemental same-test evidence. No conversions. Document identity verified: Goals as Reference Points, Heath/Larrick/Wu, Cognitive Psychology 38 (1999), article ID cogp.1998.0708. Input names no PDF; PDF layout inspection is unavailable.
